title: A Mulberry Tree Grew Lotus — So They Built This Temple | Quanzhou | China Travel Expert
description:
Legend says a mulberry tree bloomed with white lotus flowers — and that miracle is why one of China's great temples exists.

Kaiyuan Temple in Quanzhou, Fujian, was founded in 686 AD during the Tang dynasty. The story goes that a landowner, Elder Huang, donated his mulberry orchard to build the temple after his trees mysteriously bloomed white lotus. A 1,300-year-old mulberry — the "World Mulberry King" — still grows in the grounds. The temple's twin stone pagodas, Zhenguo and Renshou, were rebuilt in stone during the Song dynasty and are the tallest surviving pair of stone pagodas in China; they withstood a devastating earthquake around magnitude 8 in 1604 and still dominate the skyline. Kaiyuan is part of Quanzhou's UNESCO World Heritage listing as a great emporium of the maritime Silk Road.

🧭 Expert Tip: Walk a slow circle around the East Pagoda — its five tiers are carved with 80 stone figures, and the detail only reveals itself up close.
